```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Telemetry export pipeline"

node poller "Poller"
node normalizer "Normalizer"
node healthprobe "Health Probe"
node buffer "Ring Buffer"
node exporter "Exporter"

edge poller -> normalizer
edge healthprobe -> normalizer
edge normalizer -> buffer
edge buffer -> exporter
```

Notes:

- Genre chosen: `block` — this is a small architecture/dataflow diagram (five components, directed connections), which is exactly what `block` is for.
- Five nodes use the required ids (`poller`, `normalizer`, `healthprobe`, `buffer`, `exporter`) with short human-readable labels; per the "keep labels short" guidance, no extra detail (timers, schema shape, remote collector identity) was stuffed into the node labels — that belongs in surrounding prose if this is embedded in a doc.
- Exactly the four edges the description implies are drawn: poller→normalizer, healthprobe→normalizer, normalizer→buffer, buffer→exporter. No `class` styling was added since the description gives no distinguishing meaning (e.g., "critical path," "async," etc.) worth asserting — adding color/emphasis without a stated meaning would violate the "class is how meaning survives" rule.
- The remote collector the exporter ships to isn't a component with defined behavior in the source description (it's the destination, not one of the five named parts), so it was left out rather than invented as a sixth node.
- I don't have `reference/scene.md`/`reference/layout.md` loaded in this session, so node/edge syntax here follows the general patterns shown in the skeleton doc (quoted labels, bare ids, `->` edges). If your local `build-svg.js` reports a line error on `node`/`edge` spelling, it will name the correct replacement per the "retired spellings are hard errors" rule — rerun with that message and I'll fix the syntax accordingly.
